text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

WHEAT SALE - The Philippines bought about 24,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat early this week, exporters said. The deal consisted of 18,000 tonnes of 14 percent protein Dark Northern Spring wheat off the west coast at about $192.00 a tonne, FOB, and 6,000 tonnes of Western White wheat at about $150 to $160 a tonne, FOB, one U.S. exporter said. The exporter said shipments were slated for spot and first half April out of Portland, Oregon.

BARLEY SALE - Saudi Arabia appears to have lined up purchases of 500,000 tonnes of optional-origin barley at around $152 per tonne and above, but the deal is subject to final confirmation from Riyadh, which is expected later on Wednesday. The barley is for delivery in late April and May.

Turkey's state grain board said it did not participate in a Saudi Arabian tender under which the Arab nation will buy 500,000 tonnes of feed barley. The Canadian Wheat Board sought to sell 150,000 of Saudi Arabia's 500,000 tonne feed barley tender, trade sources said. But the CWB declined to confirm or deny the trade rumor.

RICE TENDER - Costa Rica will tender April 30 for 26,500 tonnes optional origin long grain rough rice or 18,000 tonnes long grain milled rice, U.S. number 3 or equivalent, maximum 15 percent broken, exporters and traders said. The rice was slated for June 30-July 7 arrival. But one exporter said offers have to be in by April 16 rather than April 30.
- Syria seeks 12,000 tonnes of white rice for shipment between April 20 and May 20. April 8 is the final date for bids and result will be announced on April 16.
WHEAT TENDER - USDA's Commodity Credit Corp said Tuesday it will tender April 15 to buy 25,470 tonnes northern spring wheat for donation to Ghana. The wheat will be for May 1-25 shipment.

- Negotiations are under way to sell 100,000 tonnes of North American wheat to Algeria but details are scarce on the progress of the tender which is at its working stage, European grain traders said. Algeria launched a snap tender on Tuesday for what European traders said involved four 25,000-tonne shipments of U.S. or Canadian wheat for late May and early June. "Nothing is getting out on this yet. There are very few people involved in this one," one trader said.
BARLEY TENDER - The South African Wheat Board said it was offering 25,150 tonnes of feed grade barley for export sale no later than April 30.

VEGOIL TENDER - El Salvador was seeking about 4,500 to 5,500 tonnes of U.S. vegoil under the PL-480 Title I export program, according to its shipping agent, International Services Corp. The vegoil included prime bleachable summer yellow (PBSY) cottonseed oil in bulk and/or refined bleached deodorized soybean oil in bulk. Shipping dates were slated for April 21-May 6. Offers are to be received no later than April 14 and all offers must remain valid through April 15.

TALLOW TENDER - El Salvador was tendering for about 2,000 to 3,000 tonnes of U.S. tallow in bulk under the PL-480 Title I export program, its shipping agent said. Shipment was set for April 21-May 6. Offers are to be received no later than April 14 and all offers must remain valid through April 15.
SOYMEAL TENDER - El Salvador was tendering for about 8,000 to 10,000 tonnes of U.S. soybean meal in bulk under the PL-480, Title I export program, its shipping agent said.
The meal was set for April 21-May 6 delivery. Offers are to be received by April 14 and will remain valid on April 15.

RAPESEED TENDER - A South Korean buyer group known as Big Reed Mills passed on tenders to buy 25,500 tonnes of Indian rapeseed meal due to high offer prices, officials of the buyer group said on Wednesday.

MARKET TALK - The Southeast Asian grains and oilseeds business was quiet this week with Indonesian feedmills sitting on the sidelines in a lukewarm response to Chinese corn offers. Traders in Indonesia said there were offers of Chinese corn at US$152-$155 a tonne C&F but there had been no takers.

... Egypt and Iran are expected back in the world grain market soon to buy wheat for May and June but neither has yet said officially what its needs will be, European exporters said on Wednesday. Pending tender announcements, however, most exporters said they saw scope for sales of about 200,000 tonnes to Iran and 200,000 to 300,000 tonnes to Egypt.
.. India will import a total of two million tonnes of wheat in fiscal 1997/98 (April-March). a senior government official said.
